title: Simple and compound interest
goal: I can calculate simple and compound interest.
teach: Simple interest is earned only on the original amount: A = P(1 + in). Compound interest is earned on the interest too: A = P(1 + i)ⁿ. P is the principal, i the rate as a decimal and n the number of periods.

ex.q: R4 000 is invested at 6% p.a. for 5 years. Find the amount with simple and with compound interest.

watch:
Change the percentage to a decimal: 6% = 0,06.

Problem-solving lens
Ask first: is interest earned on interest? That decides simple or compound.

qs.text: R6 000 at 9% p.a. simple interest for 3 years
qs.steps:
1. Formula (simple interest): A = P(1 + in), where P = principal, i = rate as a decimal, n = number of years.
2. A = 6 000(1 + 0,09 × 3) = 6 000 × 1,27
3. = R7 620,00

qs.text: R6 000 at 9% p.a. compounded annually for 3 years
qs.steps:
1. Formula (compound interest): A = P(1 + i)ⁿ. If interest is added m times a year, use i ÷ m as the rate and n × m periods.
2. A = 6 000(1,09)³ = 6 000 × 1,295029
3. = R7 770,17

qs.text: R3 000 grows to R3 900 in 5 years at simple interest. Find the rate.
qs.hint: Find the interest first, then use interest = P × i × n.
qs.steps:
1. Formula (simple interest): A = P(1 + in), where P = principal, i = rate as a decimal, n = number of years.
2. Interest = 3 900 − 3 000 = R900
3. 900 = 3 000 × i × 5 = 15 000i
4. i = 900 ÷ 15 000 = 0,06 = 6%
